title: Separate business and personal finances on day one
summary: Distinct business checking, business savings, dedicated business credit card. Mixing the two is the #1 mistake of new contractors.
detailsHtml:
Why this matters

Commingled finances create three immediate problems: (1) you lose audit defense — if the IRS examines your return, undifferentiated bank accounts make it impossible to substantiate business expenses; (2) you lose legal protection if you've formed an LLC, since piercing the corporate veil starts with showing commingled funds; (3) you lose visibility into actual business profitability, because personal spending masks the true margin of the business.

The minimum setup

One business checking account (income deposits + business expenses). One business savings account (tax reserve + business EF). One business credit card (everything that's a business expense, paid from business checking). Personal accounts kept entirely separate. Transfer to personal accounts as "owner draws" on a regular schedule rather than as needed.
